meta.title: Dashboards: The Warehouse ID Is Embedded, Not Attached

views.label: Rewrite before create
views.note: A Lakeview dashboard carries its datasets and warehouse ID inside its own definition, not as a separate attachment.

views.label: Strip server-owned fields
views.note: dashboard_id, create_time, update_time, etag, and lifecycle_state all belong to the source, not the target.

views.label: Renders cleanly, fails on every query
views.note: A dashboard with an un-rewritten warehouse_id imports fine, shows its layout, and fails or silently queries the wrong warehouse.

cards.title: The warehouse ID is embedded, not attached
items: A Lakeview dashboard carries its datasets and warehouse_id inside its own definition
Recreating without rewriting that ID produces a dashboard that imports cleanly and fails on every query
Or, if a warehouse with that ID happens to exist in target, it quietly runs against the wrong one

cards.title: Same workspace-scoped-ID problem as everywhere else
items: Strip dashboard_id, create_time, update_time, etag, and lifecycle_state before posting to target
The create flag is --json with an @path, not --json-file
The same pattern as queries, jobs, and pipelines: resolve the target ID, never carry the source one

cards.title: Visual parity is more than 'it opens'
items: Render migrated and source dashboards side by side for the same date range and filters
Date/time filters and aggregation defaults are where timezone and shape differences hide
For external BI tools, confirm the connection points at target — a cached schema can look connected while still querying source
